scope: Two public-source engineering evidence investigations, not two prospective reactor trials. Review claims are constructed; measurements are attributed published values.

cases.title: Hollow-anode oxygen accounting and material-performance review
cases.question: Review oxygen accounting and material-performance evidence for the 12-hour cell. Identify which supplied claims survive the evidence, which mechanisms remain alternatives, and what evidence should be acquired next before endorsing lifetime or efficiency conclusions.
cases.configuration: Yu et al. 2025 inverted hollow-anode laboratory cell, LHS-1, YSZ/Pt anode and Mo cathode. Not KSC LR-1.

sources.facts: Nominal constant current 0.5 A; 12-hour electrolysis; collected/reported oxygen mass 0.749 g. These scalars are not a raw current or calibrated outlet-flow trace.

Authors treat measured outlet oxygen as a lower bound, discussing internal oxygen production, Mo oxidation and condensed products outside the sampled gas. This is a source-specific interpretation, not a measured loss fraction.

At 1600 C, 12-hour-cell resistance changes from 1.46 to 0.78 ohm. Authors discuss electronic conductivity in YSZ; decreasing electrical resistance is not itself a measurement of improved oxygen collection efficiency.
12 hours electrolysis corresponds to 14 hours at 1600 C; wall recession 85 +/- 19 micrometres. Preserve the two time bases and printed uncertainty notation; do not assume a confidence level.
Approximately 214-hour service life is an extrapolation using constant production/recession assumptions, not a 214-hour endurance experiment. Further testing is required.

review_claims.text: The 12-hour electrolysis specimen experienced 14 hours at 1600 C.
The 12-hour cell resistance increased from its initial value.
The approximately 214-hour lifetime was demonstrated by an endurance test.
The authors report the outlet measurement as a complete oxygen-generation balance, rather than a lower bound.
The resistance decrease alone proves that oxygen-collection efficiency improved.
The authors treat measured outlet oxygen as a lower bound rather than an independently closed total-generation balance.

missing_records: Long-duration endurance evidence for lifetime claims
limits: Published development source already inspected; not a blind holdout
Four-electron charge bound is conditional arithmetic, not an independently predicted oxygen yield
No kinetic, corrosion-lifetime or calibrated fault-probability model
cases.rights: NTRS notes portions may be copyright protected. Attribute factual transcriptions; do not redistribute source PDF/figures without applicable rights review.

cases.title: LR-1 core characterization and oxygen-report comparability review
cases.question: Review post-test core characterization and related production summaries. Separate what was observed from analytical limitations and unresolved causal claims. Draft the next evidence request without transferring hollow-anode lifetime claims to LR-1.
cases.configuration: KSC ASSIST/Lunar Resources LR-1 December 2024 vacuum demonstration and retrieved core. Related 2025 poster and 2026 NTRS abstract are not independent trials.

sources.facts: Poster describes 25 kg of ICN-LHT-1G simulant processed in vacuum and reports average oxygen production around 0.1 kg/h. Retrieved-core characterization reports anode-material degradation observations. This is different hardware from the Yu hollow-anode cell.

sources.locator: Core Slice Average table, heading Atom/Mol%
sources.facts: Core-slice average Nb is printed as 10.09 under Atom/Mol%, with printed standard deviation 7.32. This basis is not weight percent; local heterogeneous core analysis is not an entire-batch composition assay.
The poster explicitly reports XPS scans as inconclusive and proposes an explanation involving Nb/x-ray absorption. That proposed explanation is not a validated universal cause.

sources.locator: Summary porosity bullet; Computed Tomography section
sources.facts: Poster reports approximately 14.84% macroporosity. Its Summary attributes the estimate to EDS, whereas the CT section describes graphically estimating macroporosity by summing slice void space. Retain this attribution ambiguity instead of silently choosing a method.

Abstract describes LR-1 processing 25 kg with approximately 0.07 kg/h average oxygen production over 9 hours of electrolysis. Slide download not verified in this packet. Matched averaging windows/calibration connecting this value with the poster's 0.1 kg/h are not supplied.

review_claims.text: The core-slice table reports Nb as 10.09 on an Atom/Mol% basis.
The reported Nb value is therefore 10.09 weight percent.
The poster reports XPS scans as conclusive.
The poster attributes macroporosity to CT consistently and never mentions EDS as the estimation method.
The two production-rate summaries alone establish reactor degradation.
The KSC poster documents observations attributed to anode degradation in the retrieved core.

missing_records: Matched reporting/averaging windows and gas calibration
Independent degradation diagnostics for a production-rate causal claim
limits: Related KSC publications grouped as one test family
Summary-rate arithmetic is not a time-series degradation measurement
XPS failure mechanism and next-experiment optimality are not established
cases.rights: Poster has a restricted NTRS reuse notice; link and attribute facts. 2026 NTRS record states Public Use Permitted. No source figures are bundled.
